statusSet.label: The status set
statusSet.reason: The contract still carries the old six statuses, so completed, problem, lost and return can never be anything but 0, and Processed counts but cannot narrow the table.

summaryCost.label: Purchase value and margin
summaryCost.reason: The per-status census sums the order total and nothing else, so the goods’ value, the cost and the count of orders with no cost are sample figures.

summaryItems.label: Item count and UPT
summaryItems.reason: The list returns no order lines and nothing counts them server-side, so both are sample figures.

export.label: Export
export.reason: Nothing builds a file yet — which columns, and whether it is this page or every row the filters match, is still open.

import.label: Import
import.reason: The file is named on screen and goes no further: no upload, no parser, and each marketplace needs its own.

warehouseFilter.label: Warehouse filter
warehouseFilter.reason: The list filter has no warehouse field, so picking one leaves the table as it was.

creator.label: Who created the order
creator.reason: An order records no creator at all — the filter narrows nothing, and the name under each date is invented.

mpDate.label: Marketplace order date
mpDate.reason: An order stores only when WE wrote it down; the date the buyer ordered on the storefront has no field, so the second line under the date is invented.

stageDate.label: Status change date
stageDate.reason: The order event already has the right shape (kind + when), but events are only sent with an order's detail — the list cannot read when an order entered the status you are filtering by.

receiptCode.label: Tracking number
receiptCode.reason: The order stores the courier and the receipt FILE, but not the number printed on the slip — the one shown is invented and will not be found by any courier.

deadline.label: Ship-by deadline
deadline.reason: Nothing carries one: the order has no deadline, the shipment channel has no lead time, and an order event records what happened rather than what is due. Every badge in the column is invented, and its colour bands are a guess.

totalFee.label: Warehouse fee in the total
totalFee.reason: The total is the goods plus what fulfilling them costs, and nothing carries that fee per order: it is a liability entry keyed by order, and the liability list can only be asked by counterparty. The goods are real, the fee is a sample.

lifecycle.label: Actions after shipping
lifecycle.reason: The contract writes only cancel and ship, so Return Goods, Complete Order, Mark as Lost and Resolve Dispute have nothing to call — the same half of the lifecycle whose four status tabs read 0.

marketplaceFilter.label: Marketplace filter
marketplaceFilter.reason: Not on the list filter either — it would mean every shop on that marketplace.

withdrawal.label: Withdrawal value
withdrawal.reason: A wallet-to-bank withdrawal is a shop-level cash event naming no order, so nothing in the system has a home for it yet — not even settlement, where every entry must name one.

shipping.noTracking: No tracking trail recorded. Most orders have none — nothing reads the courier back yet.

statusSet.label: The eight statuses
statusSet.reason: The contract still carries the old six, so Completed, Problem, Lost and Return can never appear — here or on the timeline.

notes.label: Notes
notes.reason: An order stores ONE note, written when it is created — no list, no author, no system or user type, and no way to edit it. Notes added or edited here disappear on reload.

productImage.label: Product picture
productImage.reason: An order line carries sku and name but no cover. The picture is not missing from the system, only from this message — the fix is a batched product lookup, not a new field.

externalName.label: Marketplace product title
externalName.reason: The order draft keeps the title the marketplace gave each product — the evidence a mapping is checked against — but an order line has no field for it, so promoting a draft throws it away. The titles shown are invented.

totalFee.label: Warehouse fee in the system total
totalFee.reason: Nothing carries the fee per order: it is a liability entry keyed by order, and the liability list can only be asked by counterparty. The product total is real, the fee is a sample.

deadline.label: Ship-by deadline
deadline.reason: Nothing carries one — not the order, not the shipment channel. The badge is invented.

receiptCode.label: Tracking number
receiptCode.reason: The order stores the courier and the receipt FILE, but not the number printed on the slip. The one shown is invented.

shippingTracking.label: Tracking trail
shippingTracking.reason: Where the parcel is, when it was scanned, what it weighed and what the postage cost are not modelled at all. The owner expects this section to be empty most of the time.

returnShipment.label: Return shipment
returnShipment.reason: A returned parcel travels under its own courier, tracking number and trail, and none of that exists: there is no return record at all yet. Shown for one order only, invented.

withdrawal.label: Withdrawals into the settlement ledger
withdrawal.reason: Nothing imports the marketplace's withdrawals yet, so a payout only appears in the ledger when somebody posts it by hand, and Edit Withdrawal has no RPC.

lifecycle.label: Actions after shipping
lifecycle.reason: The contract writes only cancel and ship, so Return Goods, Complete Order, Mark as Lost and Resolve Dispute have nothing to call.

orderSettlement.previewIn: This will add {{amount}} to the order.
orderSettlement.previewOut: This will take {{amount}} from the order.
orderSettlement.occurredHelp: The day the charge belongs to, not today. The day it was recorded is stamped separately.

terms.title: Credit Terms
terms.intro: What you charge each team, and how far you let them run. A balance is never due — the limit is the only control, so lowering it is also the only way to ask for money.
terms.defaultRowHelp: Applies to every team without terms of their own
terms.limitHelp: Unlimited and Frozen are opposites, not degrees. Frozen refuses the next order whatever the balance.
terms.handlingFeeHelp: Flat, per order. Nothing set means you charge nothing.
terms.reasonRequired: Required — you are changing another team's terms.
terms.reasonOptional: Optional. Recorded in the change log either way.

removeDialog.title: Remove Terms for {{name}}
removeDialog.message: This pair falls back to your DEFAULT terms — limit, fee and markup together, because the whole row is what resolves. With no default row set, that means unlimited credit.

terms.empty: No terms set. Every team you trade with is unlimited and charged nothing.
terms.tileNearHelp: At 80% or more of what you allowed
terms.noneSet: No terms set — unlimited credit, no fee, no markup

shipmentChannels.title: Shipment Channels
shipmentChannels.name: Name
shipmentChannels.codeHelpCreate: Lowercase key the third-party app maps onto (e.g. "jne"). It can never be changed.
shipmentChannels.codeHelpEdit: The code can never be changed.
shipmentChannels.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? It disappears from pickers, but past orders keep showing it. You can restore it later.

pending.title_one: {{count}} part of this screen is not implemented yet
pending.title_other: {{count}} parts of this screen are not implemented yet
pending.lead_one: One of them works on screen only — what you type into it is not sent: {{parts}}.
pending.lead_other: These work on screen only — what you type into them is not sent: {{parts}}.

bundle.label: Bundle grouping
bundle.reason: A bundle places its products as ordinary lines; the grouping itself is not stored.

returnMap.label: Return mapping
returnMap.reason: The product link map is not built.

creditLimit.label: Debt limits
creditLimit.reason: A team cannot read the limit another team set for it yet.

profit.label: Estimated profit
profit.reason: The formula is not settled, and the sell price is stored as a note.

shippingCost.label: Shipping cost
shippingCost.reason: Nothing prices a shipment, so the field is off the screen and the total is short a term.

warehouseFee.label: Warehouse fee
warehouseFee.reason: This screen does not read the warehouse's terms yet.

invoice.label: Invoice
invoice.reason: It needs each team's markup and the warehouse fee.

orderDate.label: Order date
orderDate.reason: An order is dated when it was typed in, and has no field for when it was actually bought.

deadline.label: Order deadline
deadline.reason: The order has no field for it.

buyerUsername.label: Buyer username
buyerUsername.reason: The order has no field for it.

receiptCode.label: Tracking number
receiptCode.reason: The order stores the courier and the receipt file, but not the number itself.

receiptScan.label: Receipt file check
receiptScan.reason: Nothing reads the uploaded file yet, so the autofill and the match check stand on a stand-in.

refsDistinct.label: Order ID vs tracking number
refsDistinct.reason: The comparison runs here; the authoritative checker is not built.

formatRules.label: Courier & marketplace formats
formatRules.reason: The patterns are provisional — they warn, they never refuse.

draftKeeps.label: What a draft keeps
draftKeeps.reason: A draft stores the shop, the warehouse, the customer, the courier and the rows. The receipt, the references, the tracking number, the note, the dates and the buyer's username are not kept.

rowBundle.label: A row mapped to a bundle
rowBundle.reason: A draft line holds one product, so a bundle mapping is shown and counted but saved unmapped, and it blocks Promote.

rowSplit.label: A row split into several products
rowSplit.reason: A draft line holds one product, so a split is shown and counted but saved unmapped, and it blocks Promote.

makeBundle.label: Make it a bundle
makeBundle.reason: Bundle templates are still a sample, so there is nowhere to save a new one.

sellPrice.label: The sell price
sellPrice.reason: A draft has no sell price. It starts as the sum of the rows' marketplace prices and can be typed over, but a typed one is not kept.

listingQty.label: The listing's quantity
listingQty.reason: A draft line holds one quantity, so a count that differs from the listing replaces it on save — the listing's own number and this warning are gone when the draft is opened again.

source.title: Order Information
source.help: Which storefront sold it, which warehouse ships it, and when it was bought.
source.orderDateHelp: When the customer bought it — not when it was typed in.
source.sellPriceHelp: What the customer paid on the marketplace. The margin below is measured against it.

bundles.title: Bundles
bundles.help: A bundle puts its products on the order. Each slot can be filled with something else — what it may hold is the bundle's own rule times how many bundles were ordered.

returnMap.title: Return Mapping
returnMap.help: A product ordered from another team is mapped to one of ours, so a return has somewhere to land. Answer it once and it comes back filled in next time.
returnMap.empty: Nothing on this order belongs to another team.

extra.title: Extra Details
extra.help: Optional, and neither is part of an order yet.
extra.buyerUsernameHelp: Who bought it, as the storefront shows them.

credit.title: Debt Limits
credit.help: One row per team this order would owe — the warehouse that ships it, and each team whose products are on it. An order is refused when the debt already stands at the limit.
credit.empty: Choose a warehouse to see what this order would owe.
credit.wouldPass: over the limit after this order

profit.title: Estimated Profit
profit.help: What is left of the sell price after the order's own cost. The floor is {{pct}}%.
profit.noSellPrice: No sell price yet — fill in what the storefront took, on the Order Information card.

totals.title: Total & Invoice
totals.help: What the order is worth, and how much of it is owed to somebody else.
totals.invoiceEmpty: Nothing owed — every product is this team's own.
totals.feeNote: Flat fee for fulfilling this order.
totals.costUnknown: This warehouse has no cost recorded for these goods, so nothing is billed yet.
totals.blockedByMapping: {{count}} of these products still have no return mapping — it is not saved with the order yet.

resi.title: Shipping Receipt
resi.help: The receipt file, and the two numbers printed on it.
resi.bothPrinted: The order ID and the tracking number are both on the receipt file.
resi.halfMissing: The receipt file carries both numbers — one of the boxes above is still empty.
resi.filledFromFile: Filled in from the receipt file — check it against the paper.
resi.pdfNoPreview: PDF — open it to read the numbers

checks.blockedTitle: This order cannot be placed yet
checks.blockedLead: One of these has to be corrected first.
checks.warnLead: Nothing here stops the order — read them, then decide.
checks.refsIdentical: The order ID and the tracking number are the same. They are two different references — an order carrying one of them twice cannot be found again from either side.
checks.refsNearlyIdentical: The order ID and the tracking number are nearly the same. One of them was probably pasted into both boxes.
checks.scanBothOff: Neither number matches the receipt file, which reads {{ref}} and {{code}}.
checks.scanRefOff: The order ID does not match the receipt file, which reads {{ref}}.
checks.scanCodeOff: The tracking number does not match the receipt file, which reads {{code}}.
checks.trackingCourier: The tracking number does not look like this courier's — it normally reads {{shape}}.
checks.refMarketplace: The order ID does not look like this marketplace's — it normally reads {{shape}}.
checks.profitBelowFloor: The estimated margin is {{pct}}%, under the {{floor}}% floor.

warehouse.title: Shipping from
warehouse.governs: Every stock figure and HPP below is this building's.
warehouse.chooseFirst: Choose the warehouse first — nothing below can be measured without it.

items.help: What the app read off the marketplace, one listing per row — map each to a product, a bundle, or several products.
items.addedHelp: A row the app did not read — nothing scraped to compare against.
items.splitHelp: Each product at a quantity per listing unit — the row's quantity multiplies it.

orderDraftForm.sellPriceHelp: The sum of the marketplace price on every row — what the buyer paid, and what the profit is measured against.

gaps.unmapped: A row is not mapped yet
gaps.notStorable: A bundle or split row cannot be promoted yet

statusSet.label: Handed over
statusSet.reason: Handed over is the warehouse's last step, but the contract has no status for it yet — its tab cannot narrow anything.

creator.label: Created by
creator.reason: An order records no creator — only the team it was placed for.

shop.label: The seller's shop
shop.reason: The order carries only the shop id, and a warehouse cannot read the seller's shops.

receiptCode.label: Tracking number
receiptCode.reason: The order stores the courier, not the printed tracking number.

quantity.label: Quantity
quantity.reason: A list result carries no items, so the row cannot count units.

mpDate.label: Marketplace date
mpDate.reason: The order has no field for when the buyer ordered on the marketplace.

deadline.label: Ship-by deadline
deadline.reason: No order carries a ship-by deadline yet.

teamFilter.label: Team filter
teamFilter.reason: The order list has no seller-team filter yet — picking a team narrows nothing.

marketplaceFilter.label: Marketplace filter
marketplaceFilter.reason: The order list has no marketplace filter yet — picking one narrows nothing.

courierFilter.label: Courier filter
courierFilter.reason: The order list has no courier filter yet — picking one narrows nothing.

shipmentStatus.label: Shipment state
shipmentStatus.reason: Whether a handed-over parcel is moving belongs to a shipment record, which does not exist yet.

stepMove.label: Moving a step
stepMove.reason: The server only moves an order one step forward. Skipping a step, moving back, or moving into Picked does nothing yet.

resiLookup.label: Finding by tracking number
resiLookup.reason: No RPC finds an order by its tracking number, so the handover scan looks only in the orders this screen has loaded.

bulkHandover.label: Bulk handover
bulkHandover.reason: There is no bulk handover RPC — a mass pickup hands the parcels over one call at a time.

barcode.label: Barcode
barcode.reason: Products have no barcode yet, so the validation scan matches each item's SKU.

printMerge.label: Printing labels together
printMerge.reason: Nothing merges several receipt files into one document yet.

exportFile.label: Export
exportFile.reason: There is no export RPC yet.

row.selectAll: Select every order on this page

back.title: Return to Confirmed
back.warning: The order goes back to the queue and its progress is undone. Nothing on the shelf changes — the goods were counted out when the order was placed.
back.reasonPlaceholder: Item not found on the shelf, damaged, …

scan.placeholder: Scan, or type and press Enter

handover.title: Hand Over to Courier
handover.massOn: Scans collect into the list; hand them over together.
handover.massOff: Each good scan is handed over at once.
handover.empty: Scan a parcel's label to begin.

find.title: Find This Parcel
find.help: Scan the labels in the pile until one sounds a match.

validate.title: Scan to Validate
validate.help: Scan every item. The step can move on once every line is exact.

settlementImports.title: Settlement Imports
settlementImports.subtitle: Each shop's platform statement, uploaded daily and posted to the settlement ledger row by row.
settlementImports.empty: No statement has been imported yet.
settlementImports.interruptedHint: The server stopped mid-file. Upload the same file again to finish it — rows already posted are kept.

tally.postedToShop_one: {{count}} to the shop — no order found
tally.postedToShop_other: {{count}} to the shop — no order found

dialog.title: Import Settlement File
dialog.fileHelp: The statement exactly as the platform exports it. Import every day, so each day's money lands on its own day.
dialog.notXlsx: Choose the .xlsx file the platform exported.
dialog.tooLarge: The file is larger than 10 MB.
dialog.unsupported: Only Shopee and TikTok statements can be imported for now.
dialog.keepsGoing: You can close this window — the import keeps going, and the list shows where it got to.

detail.notFound: This file is not in your team's imports.
detail.periodUnread: The statement's period is not read yet
detail.failed: The whole file was refused — nothing was posted
detail.heldNote: These rows could not post. Once the reason is fixed, upload the same file again — only these rows go in.
detail.skippedNote: These rows are not recorded, by design — they repeat money another row already carries, or a withdrawal that did not go through.
detail.toShopNote: These rows name an order that was not found, so they went to the shop. An order entered later does not receive them.

reason.unmappedType: A type nobody has mapped yet
reason.fractionalAmount: A fraction of a rupiah — never rounded
reason.failedWithdrawal: A withdrawal that did not succeed

financialAccounts.title: Accounts
financialAccounts.selectTeam: Pick a team to see its accounts.
financialAccounts.subtitle: What the team holds, and where. A balance moves only with a row — open an account to read them.

report.title: Account Report
report.subtitle: What moved the team's money, by the day it moved. Always up to date with the balances.
report.rangeInvalid: Pick a start and an end, the start first.

financialAccounts.searchPlaceholder: Search a name, holder or number
financialAccounts.notFound: This account is not in this team.
financialAccounts.empty: No accounts yet. An admin adds the team's bank, wallet and cash accounts here.
financialAccounts.belowZeroBanner_one: {{count}} account is below zero. That is allowed — check it against the bank.
financialAccounts.belowZeroBanner_other: {{count}} accounts are below zero. That is allowed — check them against the bank.
financialAccounts.unknownBanner_one: {{count}} account holds withdrawals from a shop whose bank is not named yet. Open it and choose Which Account Is This?
financialAccounts.unknownBanner_other: {{count}} accounts hold withdrawals from shops whose bank is not named yet. Open each and choose Which Account Is This?
financialAccounts.unknownExplained: A withdrawal from {{shops}} arrived before anyone named its bank, so this account was made to hold it. Name the bank, or move the money into an account you already have.
financialAccounts.belowZeroExplained: Below zero in the books — usually a payment recorded before the top-up. Reconcile against the bank.

select.noOperational: No operational account — ask an admin to mark one

form.name: Name
form.nameHelp: What the team calls it — unique in the team.
form.numberHelp: The bank number, or the wallet's phone. One real account is recorded once, across every team.
form.openingHelp: Posted as the account's first row — 0 is fine.
form.fixedHelp: fixed: another number is another account

transfer.title: Transfer From {{name}}
transfer.belowZero: {{name}} will be below zero. That is allowed, and it will be warned.

capital.title: Capital — {{name}}
capital.help: The business owner's own money, put in or taken out.

reconcile.title: Reconcile {{name}}
reconcile.shows: What does the bank app show? (Rp)
reconcile.agree: The books agree — nothing is posted, the account is marked checked.
reconcile.whyHelp: Needed when there is a difference — it is the one row that can hide missing cash.

identify.title: Which Account Is This?
identify.intro: {{amount}} came in from {{shops}} before its bank was named.
identify.fill: Not recorded yet — fill it in
identify.move: It is one we already have
identify.fillHelp: This account becomes it — its rows stay, each withdrawal on its own day.
identify.moveHelp: {{amount}} moves into it, {{shops}} withdraws there from now on, and this account is archived.

archiveDialog.title: Archive {{name}}
archiveDialog.message: {{name}} holds {{amount}}. Archived, it leaves every picker and takes no row by hand; its history stays. You can restore it.

shops.title: Shops that withdraw here
shops.none: No shop withdraws into this account.
shops.moves: {{shop}} withdraws into {{from}} now — it moves to {{to}}.
shops.first: {{shop}} names no account yet — its withdrawals start landing here.
